screen_issue: "Cotización de liquidación" is a literal term; US Spanish speakers more often say "cifra de cierre" or "monto para cancelar". Meaning preserved.

english: It decides whether your trade helps you or hurts you.
spanish: Decide si su auto de intercambio le ayuda o le perjudica.
back_translation: Decides if your trade-in car helps or hurts you.
screen_issue: "Auto de intercambio" is a literal calque; US Spanish usually says "auto a cambio" or "auto usado que entrega". Back-translation adds "trade-in car" which is accurate.

english: What is the payoff on my old loan, and who pays the lender?
spanish: ¿Cuál es la liquidación de mi préstamo anterior y quién le paga al prestamista?
back_translation: What is the payoff of my previous loan and who pays the lender?
screen_issue: "Liquidación" for payoff is less common than "monto para saldar" in US Spanish, and could be read as a sale or clearance; the phrase "quién le paga al prestamista" is fine.

english: Like the final balance on a credit card before you close it.
spanish: Como el saldo final de una tarjeta de crédito antes de cerrarla.
back_translation: Like the final balance of a credit card before closing it.

english: Negative equity (upside down)
spanish: Capital negativo (deber más de lo que vale)
back_translation: Negative equity (owing more than it's worth)
screen_issue: The heading "Capital negativo" is a finance term that may confuse readers; the parenthetical gloss helps. "Capital" for equity is a regional/financial usage a general US reader may not know.

english: You owe more than the car is worth.
spanish: Debe más de lo que vale el auto.
back_translation: You owe more than the car is worth.

english: If your trade-in is worth less than you owe, the gap is added to your new loan, and you pay interest on the old car too.
spanish: Si su auto de intercambio vale menos de lo que debe, la diferencia se suma a su préstamo nuevo, y paga interés también por el auto viejo.
back_translation: If your trade-in car is worth less than what you owe, the difference is added to your new loan, and you also pay interest on the old car.

english: It can start your next loan already underwater.
spanish: Puede hacer que su siguiente préstamo ya empiece en desventaja.
back_translation: It can make your next loan already start at a disadvantage.
screen_issue: "Desventaja" is accurate; "underwater" is rendered as a general idea, which is acceptable, though the idiom "con deuda sobre el auto" would be more natural.

english: How much of my old loan is being added to this one?
spanish: ¿Cuánto de mi préstamo anterior se suma a este?
back_translation: How much of my previous loan is added to this one?

english: Like owing $12,000 on a phone plan for a phone that is now worth $8,000.
spanish: Como deber $12,000 de un plan de teléfono por un teléfono que ahora vale $8,000.
back_translation: Like owing $12,000 on a phone plan for a phone that is now worth $8,000.

english: Equity
spanish: Capital (equity)
back_translation: Equity
screen_issue: Heading is left in English with "Capital (equity)"; the Spanish term "capital" alone could be misread as the financial sense of principal or a city, and US Spanish readers may not know it.

english: The part of the car you own.
spanish: La parte del auto que es suya.
back_translation: The part of the car that is yours.

english: It is the car's value minus what you owe. Positive equity means your trade-in helps pay for the next car.
spanish: Es el valor del auto menos lo que debe. Un capital positivo significa que su auto de intercambio ayuda a pagar el siguiente.
back_translation: It is the value of the car minus what you owe. Positive equity means your trade-in car helps pay for the next one.

english: You want it to be positive.
spanish: Quiere que sea positivo.
back_translation: You want it to be positive.

english: What is my car worth compared with what I owe?
spanish: ¿Cuánto vale mi auto comparado con lo que debo?
back_translation: How much is my car worth compared to what I owe?
screen_issue: Minor: 'compared with' rendered as 'comparado con' is fine; back-translation adds 'to' only. No meaning change.

english: Like the part of a house you own after the mortgage.
spanish: Como la parte de una casa que es suya después de la hipoteca.
back_translation: Like the part of a house that is yours after the mortgage.
screen_issue: Spanish 'Como la parte de una casa que es suya' is a fragment lacking verb; acceptable as a fragment. Back-translation 'that is yours' vs 'que es suya' is equivalent. Consider 'Como la parte de una casa que usted es dueño después de la hipoteca' for clarity.

english: Actual cash value
spanish: Valor real en efectivo
back_translation: Actual cash value
screen_issue: 'Valor real en efectivo' is a literal term; US readers may not recognize 'valor real en efectivo' as the insurance term ('valor real en efectivo' is the common Spanish insurance term, so acceptable). Back-translation identical in term.

english: What your old car is worth today.
spanish: Lo que vale hoy su auto viejo.
back_translation: What your old car is worth today.

english: Dealers and insurers use it as the car's market value. Check it with more than one source, and get a quote from other buyers.
spanish: Los vendedores y las aseguradoras lo usan como el valor de mercado del auto. Revíselo en más de una fuente y pida cotizaciones a otros compradores.
back_translation: Dealers and insurers use it as the car's market value. Check it in more than one source and ask for quotes from other buyers.
screen_issue: 'Revíselo en más de una fuente' is polite usted form; 'en más de una fuente' vs 'in more than one source' fine. Minor wording difference only.

english: It sets your trade-in credit and your insurance payout.
spanish: Fija su crédito por el auto de intercambio y lo que paga el seguro.
back_translation: It sets your credit for the trade-in car and what the insurance pays.

english: How did you work out this value for my car?
spanish: ¿Cómo calculó este valor para mi auto?
back_translation: How did you calculate this value for my car?

english: Like the price a buyer would pay for your car today, not what you paid.
spanish: Como lo que pagaría hoy un comprador por su auto, no lo que usted pagó.
back_translation: Like what a buyer would pay for your car today, not what you paid.

english: Depreciation
spanish: Depreciación
back_translation: Depreciation

english: How much value the car loses.
spanish: Cuánto valor pierde el auto.
back_translation: How much value the car loses.

english: New cars lose value fastest in the first year or two. That is why a car can be worth less than you owe on it.
spanish: Los autos nuevos pierden más valor en el primer año o dos. Por eso un auto puede valer menos de lo que debe.
back_translation: New cars lose more value in the first year or two. That's why a car can be worth less than what you owe.
screen_issue: Back-translation says 'more value' for 'pierden más valor' which matches; 'lose value fastest' rendered as 'pierden más valor' is a reasonable nuance. Minor wording difference only.

english: It is the biggest hidden cost of owning a new car.
spanish: Es el mayor costo escondido de tener un auto nuevo.
back_translation: It is the biggest hidden cost of owning a new car.

english: How fast does this model lose value?
spanish: ¿Qué tan rápido pierde valor este modelo?
back_translation: How fast does this model lose value?

english: Like an ice cream cone melting. The first minutes lose the most.
spanish: Como un helado que se derrite. Los primeros minutos pierden más.
back_translation: Like an ice cream melting. The first few minutes lose more.
screen_issue: 'Como un helado que se derrite' vs 'melting' fine; back-translation drops 'cone' in Spanish source (original says ice cream cone, Spanish omits 'cono'), small meaning loss in imagery but not meaning.

english: Lease
spanish: Arrendamiento (lease)
back_translation: Lease
screen_issue: 'Arrendamiento (lease)' is clear; 'arrendamiento' is standard Spanish but US Spanish speakers commonly say 'arrendamiento' or 'leasing'; acceptable.

english: A long rental of a car.
spanish: Un alquiler largo de un auto.
back_translation: A long-term rental of a car.

english: You pay to use the car for a set time and set miles, then give it back. You do not own it at the end unless you buy it.
spanish: Paga por usar el auto durante un tiempo y unas millas fijas, y luego lo devuelve. No es suyo al final, a menos que lo compre.
back_translation: You pay to use the car for a fixed time and miles, and then you return it. It is not yours at the end, unless you buy it.
screen_issue: 'No es suyo al final' vs 'You do not own it' fine; 'a menos que lo compre' is polite usted-compatible. Minor wording difference.

english: Payments are lower than a loan, but you own nothing and pay fees at the end.
spanish: Los pagos son menores que en un préstamo, pero no es dueño de nada y paga cargos al final.
back_translation: Payments are lower than with a loan, but you own nothing and pay fees at the end.
screen_issue: 'no es dueño de nada' is slightly stronger than 'you own nothing' but equivalent; 'cargos' is a US-familiar term for fees.

english: What do I pay at signing, and what at the end?
spanish: ¿Qué pago al firmar y qué pago al final?
back_translation: What do I pay at signing and what do I pay at the end?

english: Like renting an apartment for three years. A lower monthly cost, and no ownership.
spanish: Como alquilar un apartamento por tres años. Un costo mensual menor, y sin ser dueño.
back_translation: Like renting an apartment for three years. A lower monthly cost, and without owning.
screen_issue: 'Como alquilar un apartamento' vs 'rent an apartment' fine; 'sin ser dueño' is equivalent to 'without owning'. Minor wording difference only.

english: Capitalized cost
spanish: Costo capitalizado
back_translation: Capitalized cost
screen_issue: 'Costo capitalizado' is a literal rendering; a US Spanish reader may not know the term, so the English term in parentheses would help.

english: The price the lease is based on.
spanish: El precio en el que se basa el arrendamiento.
back_translation: The price on which the lease is based.

english: It is the negotiated price of the car in a lease, plus any fees rolled in. Lower it and the payment drops.
spanish: Es el precio negociado del auto en un arrendamiento, más los cargos que se suman. Si lo baja, el pago baja.
back_translation: It is the negotiated price of the car in a lease, plus the charges that are added. If you lower it, the payment goes down.

english: It is the lease number you can negotiate.
spanish: Es el número del arrendamiento que sí puede negociar.
back_translation: It is the lease number that you can negotiate.
screen_issue: 'Es el número del arrendamiento que sí puede negociar' loses the meaning of the English: it names a lease number, not a price. The original says the capitalized cost is the number to negotiate, and 'arrendamiento' is used for 'lease', which is consistent, but the back translation shows the link to 'lease number' is ambiguous and misleading.

english: What is the capitalized cost, and is it the price we agreed?
spanish: ¿Cuál es el costo capitalizado y es el precio que acordamos?
back_translation: What is the capitalized cost and is it the price we agreed on?
screen_issue: Back translation is faithful; the Spanish is a polite question but 'acordamos' is acceptable. Minor: 'precio que acordamos' is fine.

english: Like the agreed price of the thing you are renting.
spanish: Como el precio acordado de lo que está alquilando.
back_translation: Like the agreed price of what you are renting.
screen_issue: 'alquilando' (renting) is a register/regional choice; a US Spanish reader would normally understand it, but the analogy compares a lease to renting, and the original concept 'the thing you are renting' is preserved. Slight nuance shift in 'lo que está alquilando' versus 'lo que usted alquila'.

english: Residual value
spanish: Valor residual
back_translation: Residual value

english: What the car is worth at the end of the lease.
spanish: Lo que vale el auto al final del arrendamiento.
back_translation: What the car is worth at the end of the lease.

english: The leasing company sets it, as a percent of the sticker price. A higher residual means a lower payment, since you pay only for the part that is used up. It also sets the buyout price.
spanish: La compañía lo fija, como un porcentaje del precio de etiqueta. Un residual más alto significa un pago menor, porque paga solo la parte que se gasta. También fija el precio de compra al final.
back_translation: The company sets it, as a percentage of the sticker price. A higher residual means a lower payment, because you only pay for the part that is used up. It also sets the purchase price at the end.
screen_issue: 'Residual' is rendered as 'residual' in the translation of 'residual value' context; 'precio de etiqueta' is a fair rendering of sticker price, though 'precio de lista' is more common in US Spanish. Otherwise accurate.

english: It changes the payment a lot.
spanish: Cambia mucho el pago.
back_translation: It changes the payment a lot.

english: What is the residual value, and what is the buyout price?
spanish: ¿Cuál es el valor residual y cuál es el precio de compra al final?
back_translation: What is the residual value and what is the purchase price at the end?
screen_issue: 'precio de compra al final' is a good rendering of buyout price, though 'precio de compra final' or 'precio de opción de compra' would be more natural.

english: Like the resale value of a rented bike at the end of the season.
spanish: Como el valor de reventa de una bicicleta alquilada al final de la temporada.
back_translation: Like the resale value of a rented bicycle at the end of the season.
screen_issue: 'bicicleta' is a regional choice: a US Spanish reader would know 'bicicleta' well, but 'bicicleta alquilada' is standard. Back translation adds 'bicycle', which is a faithful match.

english: Money factor
spanish: Factor de dinero
back_translation: Money factor
screen_issue: 'Factor de dinero' is a literal translation that a US Spanish reader would not know as a car-lease term; the English term should appear for clarity.

english: The interest rate on a lease, written as a tiny number.
spanish: La tasa de interés de un arrendamiento, escrita como un número diminuto.
back_translation: The interest rate of a lease, written as a tiny number.

english: A money factor of 0.0025 is about a 6% yearly rate. To compare, multiply it by 2,400. Ask for it, since dealers can mark it up.
spanish: Un factor de dinero de 0.0025 equivale a una tasa anual de alrededor de 6%. Para comparar, multiplíquelo por 2,400. Pídalo, porque el vendedor puede aumentarlo.
back_translation: A money factor of 0.0025 is equivalent to an annual rate of around 6%. To compare, multiply it by 2,400. Ask for it, because the salesperson can increase it.
screen_issue: 'pídalo' is correct polite register, but 'multiplíquelo' and the term 'tasa anual' are fine; the concern is 'aumentarlo' versus 'marcarlo', which is a nuance for 'mark it up'. Also '2,400' uses a comma as thousands separator, which is correct for US Spanish readers.

english: A small change adds up over the whole lease.
spanish: Un cambio pequeño suma en todo el arrendamiento.
back_translation: A small change adds up over the entire lease.

english: What is the money factor, and what is that as a yearly rate?
spanish: ¿Cuál es el factor de dinero y cuánto es como tasa anual?
back_translation: What is the money factor and how much is it as an annual rate?

english: Like a rental company's finance charge, written in code.
spanish: Como el cargo financiero de una empresa de alquiler, escrito en clave.
back_translation: Like the finance charge of a rental company, written in code.
screen_issue: 'Escrito en clave' (written in code) is a fair rendering; 'cargo financiero' is standard enough.

english: Acquisition and disposition fees
spanish: Cargos de inicio y de terminación
back_translation: Start-up and termination fees
screen_issue: 'Cargos de inicio y de terminación' is a literal rendering of acquisition/disposition fees; 'terminación' is a term a US Spanish reader might not know in this sense, and 'de inicio' loses the sense of 'acquisition'. 'Cargos de adquisición y de disposición' or 'cargos de apertura y de cierre' would be clearer.

english: Fees to start and to end a lease.
spanish: Cargos por empezar y por terminar un arrendamiento.
back_translation: Fees for starting and ending a lease.

english: The acquisition fee is charged at the start. The disposition fee can be charged when you return the car. Ask whether either is waived.
spanish: El cargo de adquisición se cobra al inicio. El cargo de disposición puede cobrarse cuando devuelve el auto. Pregunte si alguno se omite.
back_translation: The acquisition fee is charged at the start. The disposition fee can be charged when you return the car. Ask if any are waived.
screen_issue: The Spanish says 'Pregunte si alguno se omite' (ask whether any is omitted), which is a loose match. The back-translation reads 'Ask if any are waived', so the Spanish 'Pregunte si alguno se omite' is close but 'omite' is less idiomatic than 'se exonera'/'se elimina'; also 'cargo de disposición' is a term a US Spanish reader may not know.

english: They are part of the true cost of the lease.
spanish: Son parte del costo real del arrendamiento.
back_translation: They are part of the actual cost of the lease.

english: Which fees are due at signing, and which at the end?
spanish: ¿Qué cargos se pagan al firmar y cuáles al final?
back_translation: What fees are paid at signing and what fees are paid at the end?

english: Like a deposit and a cleaning fee on an apartment.
spanish: Como un depósito y un cargo de limpieza de un apartamento.
back_translation: Like an apartment deposit and cleaning fee.

english: Mileage allowance
spanish: Límite de millas
back_translation: Mileage limit
screen_issue: 'Límite de millas' conveys the meaning; 'allowance' is rendered as 'limit', a small wording shift that does not change meaning.

english: How many miles the lease lets you drive.
spanish: Cuántas millas le deja manejar el arrendamiento.
back_translation: How many miles the lease lets you drive.

english: Common limits are 10,000 to 15,000 miles a year. Extra miles cost money at the end, often 15 to 30 cents each.
spanish: Los límites comunes son de 10,000 a 15,000 millas al año. Las millas extra cuestan dinero al final, a menudo de 15 a 30 centavos cada una.
back_translation: Common limits are 10,000 to 15,000 miles a year. Extra miles cost money at the end, often 15 to 30 cents each.

english: Guessing too few miles is the most common lease surprise.
spanish: Calcular muy pocas millas es la sorpresa más común en un arrendamiento.
back_translation: Calculating too few miles is the most common surprise in a lease.
screen_issue: 'Calcular' for 'guessing' is slightly more formal than 'adivinar', a small wording difference.

english: What is the yearly limit, and what does each extra mile cost?
spanish: ¿Cuál es el límite anual y cuánto cuesta cada milla extra?
back_translation: What is the annual limit and how much does each extra mile cost?

english: Like a phone plan's data limit. Go over and you pay for each extra bit.
spanish: Como el límite de datos de un plan de teléfono. Si se pasa, paga por cada poquito extra.
back_translation: Like a phone plan's data limit. If you go over, you pay for each extra bit.
screen_issue: 'Poquito' is a casual, regional-feeling word for 'bit'; a US Spanish reader would understand it but it may read as colloquial.

english: Lease buyout
spanish: Compra al final del arrendamiento
back_translation: Purchase at end of lease
screen_issue: 'Compra al final del arrendamiento' is a clear description, but the back-translation 'Purchase at end of lease' drops the term 'buyout', which a reader may not connect to the English term used elsewhere.

english: Buying the car at the end of the lease.
spanish: Comprar el auto al terminar el arrendamiento.
back_translation: Buying the car when the lease ends.

english: You pay the residual value plus any fees to keep the car. It can be a good deal if the car is worth more than that.
spanish: Paga el valor residual más los cargos para quedarse con el auto. Puede ser buen trato si el auto vale más que eso.
back_translation: You pay the residual value plus fees to keep the car. It can be a good deal if the car is worth more than that.
screen_issue: 'Paga' is informal tú register; the polite usted form is 'Paga' in this context is ambiguous. 'Valor residual' is a term a US Spanish reader may not know, though it is understandable in context.

english: You get to decide at the end.
spanish: Usted decide al final.
back_translation: You decide at the end.

english: What is the buyout price?
spanish: ¿Cuál es el precio de compra?
back_translation: What is the purchase price?
screen_issue: 'Precio de compra' is clear; the earlier term 'Compra al final del arrendamiento' is not used consistently.

english: Like buying the furniture of the apartment you rented, at the end.
spanish: Como comprar los muebles del apartamento que alquiló, al final.
back_translation: Like buying the furniture from the apartment you rented, at the end.

english: Car insurance
spanish: Seguro de auto
back_translation: Car insurance

english: Protection you must carry to drive.
spanish: Protección que debe tener para manejar.
back_translation: Protection you must have to drive.
screen_issue: 'Protección que debe tener' is a small shift from 'carry' to 'tener', which is fine in meaning.

english: States require a minimum, and lenders usually require more while you owe money. The price depends on the car, your age and where you live.
spanish: Los estados exigen un mínimo, y los prestamistas suelen exigir más mientras usted debe dinero. El precio depende del auto, su edad y dónde vive.
back_translation: States require a minimum, and lenders often require more while you owe money. The price depends on the car, your age, and where you live.

english: A new car can raise the price a lot. Get quotes before you buy.
spanish: Un auto nuevo puede subir mucho el precio. Pida cotizaciones antes de comprar.
back_translation: A new car can greatly increase the price. Ask for quotes before buying.
screen_issue: 'Pida cotizaciones' is polite usted; 'cotizaciones' is a term a US Spanish reader will understand but may be less familiar than 'presupuestos' or 'precios'.

english: Can I get an insurance quote for this exact car before I sign?
spanish: ¿Puedo pedir una cotización de seguro para este auto exacto antes de firmar?
back_translation: Can I ask for an insurance quote for this exact car before I sign?
screen_issue: "Pedir" is slightly less direct than "get" but the meaning holds.

english: Like health insurance for the car. You pay each month so a big problem is not all yours.
spanish: Como un seguro médico para el auto. Paga cada mes para que un problema grande no sea todo suyo.
back_translation: Like health insurance for the car. You pay each month so that a big problem is not all yours.

english: MPG
spanish: MPG (millas por galón)
back_translation: MPG (miles per gallon)

english: Miles per gallon.
spanish: Millas por galón.
back_translation: Miles per gallon.

english: How far the car goes on a gallon of fuel. A higher number is cheaper to run. Electric cars use MPGe.
spanish: Qué tanto avanza el auto con un galón de combustible. Un número más alto es más barato de usar. Los autos eléctricos usan MPGe.
back_translation: How far the car goes with one gallon of fuel. A higher number is cheaper to use. Electric cars use MPGe.

english: Fuel is a monthly cost on top of the payment.
spanish: El combustible es un costo mensual además del pago.
back_translation: Fuel is a monthly cost in addition to the payment.

english: What is the real fuel cost for this car?
spanish: ¿Cuánto es el costo real de combustible de este auto?
back_translation: How much is the real fuel cost of this car?
screen_issue: "Cuánto es" is a bit less natural than "¿Cuál es?" but the meaning is preserved.

english: Like how many miles a tank takes you.
spanish: Como cuántas millas le rinde un tanque.
back_translation: Like how many miles a tank lasts.
screen_issue: "Le rinde" is a common idiom for how far a tank goes, but a US reader may find it slightly unfamiliar; meaning is intact.

english: Total cost of ownership
spanish: Costo total de tener el auto
back_translation: Total cost of owning the car

english: Everything the car costs, not just the payment.
spanish: Todo lo que cuesta el auto, no solo el pago.
back_translation: Everything the car costs, not just the payment.

english: The loan, insurance, fuel, repairs, tires, registration and lost value. A cheaper car with high fuel or repair costs can cost more.
spanish: El préstamo, el seguro, el combustible, las reparaciones, las llantas, el registro y el valor que se pierde. Un auto más barato con mucho combustible o reparaciones puede costar más.
back_translation: The loan, the insurance, the fuel, the repairs, the tires, the registration, and the value that is lost. A cheaper car with a lot of fuel or repairs can cost more.
screen_issue: "Llantas" is Mexican usage for tires; a US Spanish reader may know it, but "neumáticos" or "gomas" would be less regional. "Registro" is acceptable.

english: It is the fair way to compare two cars.
spanish: Es la forma justa de comparar dos autos.
back_translation: It is the fair way to compare two cars.

english: What will insurance, fuel and repairs add each month?
spanish: ¿Cuánto sumarán cada mes el seguro, el combustible y las reparaciones?
back_translation: How much will the insurance, fuel, and repairs add up to each month?

english: Like the real cost of a pet. The adoption fee is the small part.
spanish: Como el costo real de una mascota. La cuota de adopción es la parte pequeña.
back_translation: Like the real cost of a pet. The adoption fee is the small part.

english: Bumper-to-bumper and powertrain warranty
spanish: Garantía básica y del tren motriz
back_translation: Basic and powertrain warranty

english: The maker's free repair promise.
spanish: La promesa de reparación gratis del fabricante.
back_translation: The manufacturer's promise of free repair.

english: Bumper-to-bumper covers most parts for a few years. Powertrain covers the engine and transmission for longer.
spanish: La garantía básica cubre la mayoría de las piezas por unos años. La del tren motriz cubre el motor y la transmisión por más tiempo.
back_translation: The basic warranty covers most parts for a few years. The powertrain warranty covers the engine and transmission for longer.

english: Know what you already have before you buy an extended plan.
spanish: Sepa lo que ya tiene antes de comprar un plan extendido.
back_translation: Know what you already have before buying an extended plan.

english: How long is each warranty on this car, and what does it leave out?
spanish: ¿Cuánto dura cada garantía de este auto y qué deja fuera?
back_translation: How long does each warranty for this car last and what does it leave out?

english: Like a store's repair guarantee on a new appliance.
spanish: Como la garantía de reparación de una tienda para un electrodoméstico nuevo.
back_translation: Like a store's repair warranty for a new appliance.

english: Salvage or rebuilt title
spanish: Título de salvamento o reconstruido
back_translation: Salvage or rebuilt title

english: A car once declared a total loss.
spanish: Un auto que fue declarado pérdida total.
back_translation: A car that was declared a total loss.

english: An insurer decided it cost too much to repair. It can be fixed and sold, but it is worth less and can be hard to insure.
spanish: Una aseguradora decidió que reparar costaba demasiado. Puede arreglarse y venderse, pero vale menos y puede ser difícil de asegurar.
back_translation: An insurer decided that repairing it cost too much. It can be fixed and sold, but it is worth less and can be difficult to insure.
screen_issue: Back-translation shows 'difficult' for 'hard' and 'repairing it' for 'repair'; meaning unchanged.

english: Check the history report before you buy a used car.
