spanish: Como una factura de teléfono con servicios que nunca pidió, todos mezclados en un solo número.
back_translation: Like a phone bill with services you never asked for, all mixed into a single number.
screen_issue: "factura de teléfono" is standard; "todos mezclados en un solo número" matches the back-translation. "factura" is widely understood in US Spanish.

english: 0% financing
spanish: Financiamiento al 0%
back_translation: 0% financing

english: A loan with no interest, from the maker.
spanish: Un préstamo sin intereses, ofrecido por el fabricante.
back_translation: A loan without interest, offered by the manufacturer.
screen_issue: "ofrecido por el fabricante" is accurate; back-translation "offered by the manufacturer" is close. Wording differs slightly without changing meaning.

english: The maker pays the cost of the interest to attract buyers. These offers are usually for people with very good credit, for certain models, and for shorter loans. You often cannot also take the cash rebate, so the two have to be compared.
spanish: El fabricante paga el costo de los intereses para atraer compradores. Estas ofertas suelen ser para personas con muy buen crédito, para ciertos modelos y para préstamos más cortos. Muchas veces no se puede tomar también el reembolso en efectivo, así que hay que comparar las dos opciones.
back_translation: The manufacturer pays the cost of interest to attract buyers. These offers are usually for people with very good credit, for certain models, and for shorter loans. Often you cannot also take the cash rebate, so you have to compare the two options.
screen_issue: "Muchas veces no se puede tomar también el reembolso en efectivo" uses "reembolso" for rebate, which can be confused with refund; "descuento en efectivo" or "reembolso del fabricante" would be clearer. Otherwise meaning is preserved.

english: It can save a lot, but only if the price is also fair.
spanish: Puede ahorrar mucho, pero solo si el precio también es justo.
back_translation: You can save a lot, but only if the price is also fair.

english: If I take the 0% offer, do I lose the rebate, and what would the payment be with the rebate and my own loan?
spanish: Si tomo la oferta del 0%, ¿pierdo el reembolso, y cuánto sería el pago con el reembolso y mi propio préstamo?
back_translation: If I take the 0% offer, do I lose the rebate, and how much would the payment be with the rebate and my own loan?
screen_issue: "¿cuánto sería el pago con el reembolso y mi propio préstamo?" is polite and clear. Back-translation "how much would the payment be" matches the original. Shares the "reembolso" wording issue noted above.

english: Like a shop offering you interest-free months on a sofa. It helps only if the sofa is not priced higher to pay for it.
spanish: Como una tienda que le ofrece meses sin intereses por un sofá. Ayuda solo si el sofá no tiene un precio más alto para pagarlo.
back_translation: Like a store offering you months without interest for a sofa. It only helps if the sofa doesn't have a higher price to pay for it.
screen_issue: "Como una tienda que le ofrece meses sin intereses por un sofá" uses "meses sin intereses", a common Mexican phrasing that a US Spanish reader may find less familiar than "financiamiento sin intereses"; meaning is preserved.

english: Principal
spanish: Capital del préstamo (principal)
back_translation: Loan principal
screen_issue: "Capital del préstamo (principal)" is an accurate term, but "principal" in parentheses is a lexical gloss that a US Spanish reader may not recognize; "capital" alone could be read as the city or as the financial capital. The back-translation "Loan principal" matches the English but the Spanish needs clearer framing.

english: The part of the loan that is the money you borrowed.
spanish: La parte del préstamo que es el dinero que usted pidió.
back_translation: The part of the loan that is the money you asked for.
screen_issue: "La parte del préstamo que es el dinero que usted pidió" is clear and uses polite usted; back-translation "The part of the loan that is the money you asked for" matches. Slightly wordy but accurate.

english: The principal is what you borrowed, not counting interest. Each payment pays some interest and reduces the principal a little. Early in a loan most of the payment is interest.
spanish: El capital es lo que usted pidió prestado, sin contar los intereses. Cada pago cubre algo de interés y reduce un poco el capital. Al principio del préstamo, la mayor parte del pago es interés.
back_translation: The principal is what you borrowed, not counting interest. Each payment covers some interest and reduces the principal a little. At the beginning of the loan, most of the payment is interest.
screen_issue: "Cubre" for "pays" is slightly softer than "paga", but meaning is preserved; the figure-free template is fine.

english: Only the principal going down makes you owe less.
spanish: Solo cuando el capital baja, usted debe menos.
back_translation: Only when the principal goes down, you owe less.

english: After this payment, how much of the loan will still be principal?
spanish: Después de este pago, ¿cuánto del préstamo seguirá siendo capital?
back_translation: After this payment, how much of the loan will still be principal?

english: Like the original price of what you bought on a store card, before the interest was added.
spanish: Como el precio original de lo que compró con una tarjeta de la tienda, antes de sumar los intereses.
back_translation: Like the original price of what you bought with a store card, before adding interest.

english: Finance charge
spanish: Cargo financiero
back_translation: Finance charge
screen_issue: "Cargo financiero" is a term a US Spanish reader may not recognize; the official Spanish term in the federal Truth in Lending box is usually "cargo por financiamiento".

english: What it costs in dollars to borrow the money.
spanish: Lo que cuesta en dólares pedir prestado el dinero.
back_translation: What it costs in dollars to borrow the money.

english: The finance charge is the total dollar cost of the credit over the whole loan: the interest and certain fees. It is one of the numbers in the federal loan box on the contract. A lower figure means a cheaper loan.
spanish: El cargo financiero es el costo total del crédito en dólares durante todo el préstamo: los intereses y ciertos cargos. Es uno de los números del cuadro federal del préstamo en el contrato. Una cifra menor significa un préstamo más barato.
back_translation: The finance charge is the total cost of credit in dollars over the entire loan: interest and certain charges. It is one of the numbers in the federal loan box in the contract. A lower figure means a cheaper loan.
screen_issue: "Cuadro federal del préstamo" is less clear than the original "federal loan box"; "cuadro de divulgación" or a note tying it to the Truth in Lending box would help. "Cargos" is fine.

english: It lets you compare two loans in dollars instead of in percentages.
spanish: Le permite comparar dos préstamos en dólares en lugar de en porcentajes.
back_translation: It allows you to compare two loans in dollars instead of percentages.

english: What is the finance charge on this loan, and what would it be at a lower rate or a shorter term?
spanish: ¿Cuál es el cargo financiero de este préstamo, y cuánto sería con una tasa menor o un plazo más corto?
back_translation: What is the finance charge for this loan, and how much would it be with a lower rate or a shorter term?
screen_issue: "Cuánto sería" is a slight shift from "what it would be" but the meaning is kept; minor wording only.

english: Like the extra you pay on a gadget bought on instalments, compared with paying cash.
spanish: Como lo extra que paga por un aparato comprado a plazos, comparado con pagarlo al contado.
back_translation: Like the extra you pay for an appliance bought in installments, compared to paying cash.
screen_issue: "Lo extra" is a register/grammar slip (should be "lo extra" as "el extra" or "lo adicional"); "aparato" is a regional/less common word for gadget in US Spanish, where "aparato" is generally understood but "gadget" may be better rendered as "artefacto" or "dispositivo".

english: Total of payments
spanish: Total de pagos
back_translation: Total of payments
screen_issue: "Total de pagos" is a faithful rendering, but the official Truth in Lending label in Spanish is "monto total de los pagos"; acceptable as is.

english: Every payment on the loan, added up.
spanish: Todos los pagos del préstamo, sumados.
back_translation: All loan payments, added up.

english: It is the amount you will have paid when the loan ends, if you pay on schedule. It is the amount financed plus the finance charge. It appears in the loan box on the contract.
spanish: Es lo que habrá pagado cuando termine el préstamo, si paga según lo programado. Es el monto financiado más el cargo financiero. Aparece en el cuadro del préstamo en el contrato.
back_translation: It is what you will have paid when the loan ends, if you pay as scheduled. It is the financed amount plus the finance charge. It appears in the loan box in the contract.
screen_issue: "Monto financiado" matches the box terminology; "lo programado" is fine. Overall faithful.

english: It is the real size of the commitment, not just the monthly figure.
spanish: Es el tamaño real del compromiso, no solo la cifra mensual.
back_translation: It is the real size of the commitment, not just the monthly figure.

english: What is the total of payments, and how does it change if I shorten the loan?
spanish: ¿Cuál es el total de pagos, y cómo cambia si acorto el préstamo?
back_translation: What is the total of payments, and how does it change if I shorten the loan?

english: Like the full amount on a gym contract after you add up every month of the membership.
spanish: Como el monto completo de un contrato de gimnasio, después de sumar cada mes de la membresía.
back_translation: Like the full amount of a gym contract, after adding each month of membership.
screen_issue: "Monto completo" is accurate; "membresía" is standard in US Spanish. Minor wording difference only.

english: Truth in Lending box
spanish: Cuadro de la Ley de Veracidad en los Préstamos
back_translation: Truth in Lending Act Box
screen_issue: "Ley de Veracidad en los Préstamos" is a literal rendering that a US Spanish reader may not recognize; the usual Spanish name is "Ley de Veracidad en los Préstamos (Truth in Lending)" and the box is typically called "cuadro de la Ley de Veracidad en los Préstamos"; the back-translation "Truth in Lending Act Box" is acceptable but the Spanish term should be glossed.

english: The box on the contract that shows the loan's true cost.
spanish: El cuadro del contrato que muestra el costo verdadero del préstamo.
back_translation: The box in the contract that shows the true cost of the loan.

english: Federal law requires the lender to show the APR, the finance charge, the amount financed and the total of payments in a box on the contract. These four numbers let you compare any loan fairly. Check them against what you were told.
spanish: La ley federal exige que el prestamista muestre en un cuadro del contrato la tasa APR, el cargo financiero, el monto financiado y el total de pagos. Estos cuatro números permiten comparar cualquier préstamo de manera justa. Revíselos contra lo que le dijeron.
back_translation: Federal law requires the lender to show in a box in the contract the APR, the finance charge, the financed amount, and the total of payments. These four numbers allow you to compare any loan fairly. Check them against what you were told.
screen_issue: "Cuadro" and "vale lo que dice" are fine; "tasa APR" redundantly pairs "tasa" with an English acronym that US Spanish readers know, acceptable. Minor wording only.

english: If the box does not match what you were quoted, it is the box that counts.
spanish: Si el cuadro no coincide con lo que le cotizaron, vale lo que dice el cuadro.
back_translation: If the box does not match what you were quoted, what the box says is valid.
screen_issue: "Vale lo que dice el cuadro" changes the emphasis from "it is the box that counts" to a more general validity claim and is less idiomatic; "lo que dice el cuadro es lo que cuenta" would be a closer and clearer rendering that could mislead less.

english: Can we go through the four numbers in the loan box before I sign?
spanish: ¿Podemos repasar los cuatro números del cuadro del préstamo antes de que firme?
back_translation: Can we review the four numbers from the loan box before I sign?

english: Like the price per kilo on a shelf label. It lets you compare two products that look different.
spanish: Como el precio por kilo en la etiqueta del estante. Permite comparar dos productos que se ven distintos.
back_translation: Like the price per kilo on the shelf label. It allows comparing two products that look different.
screen_issue: 'Permite' vs 'allows' is fine; 'el precio por kilo' drops 'the' but meaning is unchanged.

english: Captive lender
spanish: Financiera del fabricante
back_translation: Manufacturer's finance company
screen_issue: 'Financiera del fabricante' is clear; a US reader may not know 'captive lender' as a term, but the translation is accurate and understandable.

english: The car maker's own finance company.
spanish: La compañía de financiamiento propia del fabricante del auto.
back_translation: The car manufacturer's own financing company.
screen_issue: 'Compañía de financiamiento' is a common term; 'financiera' in the translation is standard in Latin American usage. Accurate overall.

english: Many makers have a lender that exists to finance their cars. It is the one that offers 0% and other special rates. Its regular rates are often not the lowest, so it helps to compare them with a bank or a credit union.
spanish: Muchos fabricantes tienen una financiera cuyo fin es financiar sus autos. Es la que ofrece el 0% y otras tasas especiales. Sus tasas normales muchas veces no son las más bajas, así que conviene compararlas con un banco o una cooperativa de crédito.
back_translation: Many manufacturers have a finance company whose purpose is to finance their cars. It is the one that offers 0% and other special rates. Their normal rates are often not the lowest, so it is convenient to compare them with a bank or a credit union.
screen_issue: 'Cuyo fin es financiar' is slightly more literal than the original but preserves meaning; 'cooperativa de crédito' is the standard US Spanish term for credit union and is correct.

english: Its special offers can be the best deal, and its normal ones may not be.
spanish: Sus ofertas especiales pueden ser el mejor trato, y las normales quizá no.
back_translation: Their special offers can be the best deal, and the normal ones perhaps not.
screen_issue: 'Quizá no' conveys the hedge of 'may not be'; minor wording difference only.

english: Is this rate from the maker's own lender, and what is its regular rate without the special offer?
spanish: ¿Esta tasa es de la financiera del fabricante, y cuál es su tasa normal sin la oferta especial?
back_translation: Is this rate from the manufacturer's finance company, and what is their normal rate without the special offer?

english: Like a store that offers its own credit card. The first-month deal is good, and the rate afterwards is not.
spanish: Como una tienda que ofrece su propia tarjeta. La oferta del primer mes es buena, y la tasa de después no.
back_translation: Like a store that offers its own card. The first month's offer is good, and the rate afterward is not.
screen_issue: 'Tarjeta' drops 'credit' (tarjeta de crédito) but context makes it clear; meaning preserved.

english: Credit union
spanish: Cooperativa de crédito (credit union)
back_translation: Credit union

english: A member-owned lender, often with lower rates.
spanish: Un prestamista propiedad de sus miembros, muchas veces con tasas menores.
back_translation: A lender owned by its members, often with lower rates.
screen_issue: 'Prestamista propiedad de sus miembros' vs 'owned by its members' – accurate; 'prestamista' is slightly less common than 'entidad prestamista' but understandable.

english: A credit union is a not-for-profit lender owned by its members. Car loan rates there are often lower than at banks or dealers. You usually need to join, which can be as simple as living or working in the right area.
spanish: Una cooperativa de crédito es un prestamista sin fines de lucro, propiedad de sus miembros. Las tasas de préstamo de auto allí suelen ser menores que en bancos o concesionarios. Normalmente hay que afiliarse, y a veces basta con vivir o trabajar en la zona indicada.
back_translation: A credit union is a non-profit lender, owned by its members. Auto loan rates there are usually lower than at banks or dealerships. Normally you have to join, and sometimes it is enough to live or work in the indicated area.
screen_issue: 'Sin fines de lucro' is accurate. 'Afiliarse' is a standard but somewhat formal verb; 'a veces basta con vivir o trabajar en la zona indicada' keeps the meaning. Register is neutral, not explicitly usted-form but no verb forms are addressed to the reader here.

english: A pre-approval from a credit union gives you a rate to compare with the dealer's.
spanish: Una preaprobación de una cooperativa de crédito le da una tasa para comparar con la del concesionario.
back_translation: A pre-approval from a credit union gives you a rate to compare with the dealership's.
screen_issue: 'Preaprobación' is a recognized term in US Spanish; 'le da' is polite and consistent with usted.

english: What rate would your lender offer me, and can I compare it with a credit union's pre-approval?
spanish: ¿Qué tasa me ofrecería su prestamista, y puedo compararla con la preaprobación de una cooperativa de crédito?
back_translation: What rate would your lender offer me, and can I compare it with a credit union's pre-approval?
screen_issue: The Spanish is not in the 'usted' register: the original asks 'your lender' and the translation gives a 'me ofrecería' conditional that is acceptable, but the back-translation is identical to the original, so the Spanish text itself cannot be checked here; 'preaprobación' used without explanation may confuse a US reader unfamiliar with the term.

english: Like a food co-op. The members own it, so it aims to cost its members less rather than earn a profit.
spanish: Como una cooperativa de alimentos. Los miembros son los dueños, así que busca costarles menos en lugar de ganar dinero.
back_translation: Like a food cooperative. The members are the owners, so it seeks to cost them less instead of making money.
screen_issue: 'Cooperativa de alimentos' is a reasonable equivalent for 'food co-op'; 'busca costarles menos' is accurate. Slight loss of the 'rather than earn a profit' nuance is minor.

english: Default
spanish: Incumplimiento del préstamo
back_translation: Loan default
screen_issue: 'Incumplimiento del préstamo' is accurate; a US reader will understand it, though 'default' is commonly rendered as 'incumplimiento' in finance, which is fine.

english: Falling so far behind that the lender can act.
spanish: Atrasarse tanto que el prestamista puede actuar.
back_translation: Falling so far behind that the lender can act.
screen_issue: 'Atrasarse tanto que el prestamista puede actuar' is accurate; 'atrasarse' is widely understood.

english: A loan goes into default when you break its terms, most often by missing payments for long enough. The lender can then take the car back. The exact point is in the contract, and some lenders move quickly.
spanish: Un préstamo entra en incumplimiento cuando se rompen sus condiciones, casi siempre por dejar de pagar durante bastante tiempo. El prestamista puede entonces recuperar el auto. El punto exacto está en el contrato, y algunos prestamistas actúan rápido.
back_translation: A loan goes into default when its conditions are broken, almost always by stopping payments for quite some time. The lender can then repossess the car. The exact point is in the contract, and some lenders act quickly.
screen_issue: 'Recuperar el auto' is the standard term for repossession and is clear; 'actuar rápido' is a faithful rendering.

english: It damages your credit and can leave you owing money after the car is gone.
spanish: Daña su crédito y puede dejarlo debiendo dinero cuando el auto ya no está.
back_translation: It damages your credit and can leave you owing money when the car is no longer there.
screen_issue: 'Dejarlo debiendo dinero' is correct and clear; 'cuando el auto ya no está' is a slight loosening of 'after the car is gone' but meaning is preserved.

english: How many days late before this loan counts as in default, and who do I call if I need help?
spanish: ¿Con cuántos días de atraso se considera que este préstamo está en incumplimiento, y a quién llamo si necesito ayuda?
back_translation: How many days late is this loan considered in default, and who do I call if I need help?
screen_issue: The translation drops the indirect question structure but also uses 'a quién llamo' which is acceptable; the main concern is that the Spanish 'Con cuántos días de atraso se considera' is clear, but the back-translation reads 'is this loan considered in default', which loses the 'who do I call' nuance of seeking help in a way that could be read as a request for contact rather than assistance; minor, but flagged for tone.

english: Like missing so many rent payments that the landlord can start an eviction.
spanish: Como atrasarse tantos pagos de alquiler que el dueño puede empezar un desalojo.
back_translation: Like falling so many rent payments behind that the owner can start an eviction.
screen_issue: 'Desalojo' is the standard term for eviction and is accurate; 'alquiler' is the common US Spanish word for rent and is correct.

english: Deficiency balance
spanish: Saldo deficitario
back_translation: Deficiency balance
screen_issue: Term is a standard finance term; 'saldo deficitario' is the usual Spanish term, though some US Spanish readers may not know it. Consider adding a plain explanation.

english: What you still owe after the car is sold for less.
spanish: Lo que todavía debe después de que el auto se vende por menos.
back_translation: What you still owe after the car sells for less.
screen_issue: 'se vende' versus 'sells' is a small wording difference and does not change meaning; 'Lo que todavía debe' is polite usted form.

english: If the lender takes the car and sells it for less than you owe, the difference, plus costs, is the deficiency. The lender can ask you to pay it. It can lead to collection and a court judgment.
spanish: Si el prestamista recupera el auto y lo vende por menos de lo que usted debe, la diferencia, más los costos, es el saldo deficitario. El prestamista puede pedirle que lo pague. Puede llegar a cobranza y a una sentencia judicial.
back_translation: If the lender takes back the car and sells it for less than you owe, the difference, plus costs, is the deficiency balance. The lender can ask you to pay it. It can go to collections and a court judgment.
screen_issue: 'Deficiency' is rendered as 'saldo deficitario' and 'deficitario' is an uncommon word for US readers. 'Collection' is rendered as 'cobranza', which is standard in Mexico but may be less familiar in some US Spanish; 'sentencia judicial' is clear. The Spanish says 'recupera' where English says 'takes back', which is acceptable.

english: Losing the car does not always end the debt.
spanish: Perder el auto no siempre termina la deuda.
back_translation: Losing the car does not always end the debt.

english: If the car were taken back and sold for less than I owe, would I owe the difference?
spanish: Si me quitaran el auto y lo vendieran por menos de lo que debo, ¿tendría que pagar la diferencia?
back_translation: If my car was repossessed and sold for less than I owe, would I have to pay the difference?
screen_issue: 'Me quitaran' (passive-like 'would be taken away') is a reasonable rendering of 'repossessed', though 'me recuperaran el auto' is more precise and common. Meaning preserved; usted/tú is consistent with first-person question.

english: Like selling a house for less than the mortgage. You gave up the house and still owe the bank the rest.
spanish: Como vender una casa por menos que la hipoteca. Entregó la casa y todavía le debe el resto al banco.
back_translation: Like selling a house for less than the mortgage. You gave up the house and still owe the bank the rest.

english: Payment deferral
spanish: Aplazamiento de pago
back_translation: Payment deferral
screen_issue: 'Aplazamiento de pago' is clear and standard; the English 'deferral' is also a bit formal, so this is a close match.

english: Asking the lender to skip a payment for now.
spanish: Pedirle al prestamista que se salte un pago por ahora.
back_translation: Asking the lender to skip a payment for now.

english: If you have a hard month, some lenders let you move a payment to the end of the loan. Interest usually keeps growing in the meantime, and the lender may charge a fee. It is better to ask before you miss a payment than after.
spanish: Si tiene un mes difícil, algunos prestamistas permiten mover un pago al final del préstamo. Los intereses normalmente siguen creciendo mientras tanto, y el prestamista puede cobrar un cargo. Es mejor preguntar antes de dejar de pagar que después.
back_translation: If you have a tough month, some lenders allow moving a payment to the end of the loan. Interest normally keeps growing in the meantime, and the lender can charge a fee. It is better to ask before you stop paying than after.
screen_issue: 'Mover un pago' is slightly less precise than 'aplazar'; 'cargo' for fee is clear. Meaning preserved; usted form used correctly.

english: It can keep you out of default, but it is not free.
spanish: Puede evitar que caiga en incumplimiento, pero no es gratis.
back_translation: It can keep you from defaulting, but it is not free.
screen_issue: 'Incumplimiento' is standard, but 'caiga en incumplimiento' is slightly stronger than 'defaulting'; the meaning holds.

english: If I needed to skip a payment, what would it cost me in fees and interest, and how do I ask?
spanish: Si necesitara saltarme un pago, ¿cuánto me costaría en cargos e intereses, y cómo lo solicito?
back_translation: If I needed to skip a payment, how much would it cost me in fees and interest, and how do I request it?
screen_issue: 'Cuánto me costaría' is a reasonable rendering of 'how much would it cost me'. 'Cómo lo solicito' is a fair rendering of 'how do I request it'; the 'skipping' verb 'saltarme' is informal in tone for a usted-context text but still understandable.

english: Like asking a friend to wait a month for what you owe. They may agree, and may want something extra for waiting.
spanish: Como pedirle a un amigo que espere un mes por lo que le debe. Puede aceptar, y quizá quiera algo extra por esperar.
back_translation: Like asking a friend to wait a month for what you owe them. They might agree, and they might want something extra for waiting.
screen_issue: 'Pida a un amigo' and the sentence 'le debe' are fine, but 'quizá quiera algo extra' adds a hedge that softens 'they may want something extra'; also 'Como pedirle' is a slightly casual analogy. Nuance is close but could be read more loosely than the original.

english: Debt-to-income ratio
spanish: Relación deuda-ingreso
back_translation: Debt-to-income ratio
screen_issue: 'Relación deuda-ingreso' is the standard Spanish term, though some US readers might not recognize it; no meaning change.

english: How much of your monthly income goes to debts.
spanish: Qué parte de sus ingresos mensuales se va en deudas.
back_translation: What part of your monthly income goes to debts.
screen_issue: 'Qué parte de sus ingresos mensuales se va en deudas' is accurate; the back-translation is slightly less natural but the meaning is unchanged.

english: Lenders add up your monthly debt payments, such as rent or a mortgage, cards and loans, and divide by your monthly income before tax. A lower ratio makes a lender more willing to approve you and gives a better rate.
spanish: Los prestamistas suman sus pagos mensuales de deudas, como alquiler o hipoteca, tarjetas y préstamos, y los dividen entre sus ingresos mensuales antes de impuestos. Una relación menor hace que un prestamista esté más dispuesto a aprobarlo y le dé una mejor tasa.
back_translation: Lenders add up your monthly debt payments, like rent or mortgage, cards, and loans, and divide them by your monthly income before taxes. A lower ratio makes a lender more willing to approve you and give you a better rate.
screen_issue: 'Relación menor' and the division explanation are accurate; 'pagos mensuales de deudas' is clear. 'Ingresos mensuales antes de impuestos' is correct. Minor wording differences only.

english: A big car payment can push you over a lender's limit, even with a good score.
spanish: Un pago de auto grande puede pasar el límite de un prestamista, aun con buen puntaje.
back_translation: A large car payment can pass a lender's limit, even with a good score.
screen_issue: 'Pasar el límite' versus 'push you over' is a nuance difference; 'Pago de auto grande' is a common phrase. 'Aun con buen puntaje' is fine. The back-translation 'pass a lender's limit' is slightly less idiomatic than 'push you over', which could mislead slightly about how the limit is reached.

english: What payment would keep my debt-to-income ratio in the range your lender likes?
spanish: ¿Qué pago mantendría mi relación deuda-ingreso dentro del rango que le gusta a su prestamista?
back_translation: What payment would keep my debt-to-income ratio within the range your lender likes?

english: Like checking how much of your pay is already spoken for before you take on another bill.
spanish: Como revisar cuánto de su sueldo ya está comprometido antes de aceptar otra cuenta.
back_translation: Like checking how much of your salary is already committed before agreeing to another bill.
screen_issue: 'Comprometido' rather than 'spoken for' is a reasonable rendering; 'sueldo' versus 'pay' is fine in US Spanish. 'Aceptar otra cuenta' is a slight shift from 'take on another bill' but the meaning holds.

english: Loan-to-value ratio
spanish: Relación préstamo-valor
back_translation: Loan-to-value ratio
screen_issue: The term is kept in English. A US Spanish reader may not know 'relación préstamo-valor' without explanation; the Spanish term is the common one.

english: How big the loan is compared with the car's worth.
spanish: Qué tan grande es el préstamo comparado con lo que vale el auto.
back_translation: How big the loan is compared to what the car is worth.
screen_issue: 'Qué tan grande es el préstamo comparado con lo que vale el auto' is accurate; 'lo que vale' is slightly less precise than 'worth' but the meaning is kept.

english: Divide the loan by the car's value. At 100% you borrow exactly what the car is worth. Above it, you are borrowing more than the car is worth, for instance when negative equity or add-ons are rolled in. Lenders look at it closely and may charge a higher rate when it is high.
spanish: Divida el préstamo entre el valor del auto. Con 100% pide exactamente lo que vale el auto. Por encima, pide más de lo que vale, por ejemplo cuando se suma capital negativo o extras. Los prestamistas lo miran de cerca y pueden cobrar una tasa más alta cuando es alto.
back_translation: Divide the loan by the value of the car. With 100% you ask for exactly what the car is worth. Above, you ask for more than it is worth, for example when negative equity or extras are added. Lenders look at it closely and can charge a higher rate when it is high.
screen_issue: "Ratio" is rendered as "relación" and "lenders... can charge" is fine; "capital negativo" is a common term but could be read as a financial term more than the English 'negative equity' implies, and 'extras' is a slightly loose rendering of 'add-ons'. Acceptable overall.

english: A high ratio means you start out owing more than the car is worth.
spanish: Una relación alta significa que empieza debiendo más de lo que vale el auto.
back_translation: A high ratio means you start owing more than the car is worth.

english: What is the loan-to-value on this deal, and how does it change if I put more down?
spanish: ¿Cuál es la relación préstamo-valor de este trato, y cómo cambia si doy más de enganche?
back_translation: What is the loan-to-value ratio of this deal, and how does it change if I give more down payment?
screen_issue: "Relación préstamo-valor" is a standard term, but "trato" is an informal word for 'deal' that is less standard in car-buying contexts in the US; "dar de enganche" is close to "put down" but less common than "dar un enganche". The back-translation 'give more down payment' reflects this minor wording issue.

english: Like borrowing against a house for more than it is worth. The lender takes more of a risk and you pay more for it.
spanish: Como pedir prestado sobre una casa por más de lo que vale. El prestamista corre más riesgo y usted paga más por eso.
back_translation: Like borrowing on a house for more than it is worth. The lender takes on more risk and you pay more for that.
screen_issue: "Corre más riesgo" and "paga más por eso" preserve meaning; "pedir prestado sobre una casa" is a fair rendering of 'borrowing against a house'. Slight loss of nuance in 'against' (refers to home equity borrowing) but understandable.

english: Subprime loan
spanish: Préstamo de alto riesgo (subprime)
back_translation: High-risk loan (subprime)
screen_issue: "Subprime" is kept in English and the Spanish gloss "alto riesgo" is provided; US Spanish readers may recognize the English term but "alto riesgo" is the clarifying gloss, which is acceptable.

english: A loan for people with lower credit scores.
spanish: Un préstamo para personas con puntaje de crédito más bajo.
back_translation: A loan for people with lower credit scores.

english: Lenders group borrowers by credit score. Subprime is the group with lower scores, and it pays much higher interest. Some dealers specialise in it. A subprime loan can still be a way to rebuild credit if the terms are fair and payments are made on time.
spanish: Los prestamistas agrupan a los prestatarios por puntaje de crédito. Subprime es el grupo con puntajes más bajos, y paga intereses mucho más altos. Algunos concesionarios se especializan en ellos. Un préstamo subprime puede servir para reconstruir el crédito si las condiciones son justas y los pagos se hacen a tiempo.
back_translation: Lenders group borrowers by credit score. Subprime is the group with lower scores, and pays much higher interest. Some dealerships specialize in them. A subprime loan can serve to rebuild credit if the conditions are fair and payments are made on time.
screen_issue: "Puntaje" is the common US Spanish term for credit score, good. "Agrupan" and "se especializan en ellos" are faithful. "Prestatarios" is a less common word for borrowers in US Spanish; "prestatarios" is understood but "prestatarios" may read as formal/regional. Minor.

english: The difference in total cost from a prime loan can be thousands of dollars.
spanish: La diferencia en costo total frente a un préstamo prime puede ser de miles de dólares.
back_translation: The difference in total cost versus a prime loan can be thousands of dollars.

english: What would my rate be at a bank or a credit union, and can I refinance this loan later if my score improves?
spanish: ¿Qué tasa me darían en un banco o una cooperativa de crédito, y puedo refinanciar este préstamo más adelante si mejora mi puntaje?
back_translation: What rate would a bank or credit union give me, and can I refinance this loan later if my score improves?

english: Like paying a higher insurance price after an accident. The company is pricing the risk it sees.
spanish: Como pagar más por el seguro después de un accidente. La compañía está poniendo precio al riesgo que ve.
back_translation: Like paying more for insurance after an accident. The company is pricing the risk it sees.

english: Rate shopping
spanish: Comparar tasas
back_translation: Compare rates

english: Comparing loan offers without hurting your credit.
spanish: Comparar ofertas de préstamo sin dañar su crédito.
back_translation: Compare loan offers without damaging your credit.

english: Each lender that checks your credit makes a hard inquiry. Credit scoring models usually count several car-loan inquiries made within a short window as one. The window is often 14 days, and up to 45 for some models. So you can compare offers, if you do it close together.
spanish: Cada prestamista que revisa su crédito hace una consulta fuerte. Los modelos de puntaje suelen contar varias consultas de préstamo de auto hechas en un plazo corto como una sola. El plazo suele ser de 14 días, y de hasta 45 en algunos modelos. Así puede comparar ofertas, si lo hace en fechas cercanas.
back_translation: Every lender that checks your credit makes a hard inquiry. Score models usually count several auto loan inquiries made within a short period as a single one. The period is usually 14 days, and up to 45 in some models. This way you can compare offers, if you do it on close dates.
screen_issue: "Consulta fuerte" is a literal rendering of 'hard inquiry' and is understandable but not the most common US Spanish phrasing; "plazo" for 'window' is fine. The English 'as one' and 'within a short window' are preserved.

english: It lets you shop for the best rate without being afraid of the score.
spanish: Le permite buscar la mejor tasa sin temerle al puntaje.
back_translation: It allows you to look for the best rate without fearing your score.
screen_issue: "Temerle al puntaje" is idiomatic and clear, but 'afraid of the score' becomes a slightly more colloquial 'fear' construction; meaning preserved.

english: Will this check count as one inquiry if I compare other lenders in the same two weeks?
spanish: ¿Esta consulta contará como una sola si comparo otros prestamistas en las mismas dos semanas?
back_translation: Will this inquiry count as a single one if I compare other lenders in the same two weeks?

english: Like asking three shops for a quote on the same job. It is one search, not three.
spanish: Como pedirle presupuesto a tres talleres por el mismo trabajo. Es una búsqueda, no tres.
back_translation: Like asking three workshops for a quote for the same job. It's one search, not three.
screen_issue: "Talleres" for 'shops' is a reasonable rendering in the sense of repair/service shops, though "tiendas" or "mecánicos" might be clearer; "Es una búsqueda, no tres" is faithful but slightly terse.

english: Credit insurance
spanish: Seguro de crédito
back_translation: Credit insurance

english: Insurance that pays your loan if you die or cannot work.
spanish: Un seguro que paga su préstamo si usted fallece o no puede trabajar.
back_translation: An insurance that pays your loan if you die or cannot work.
screen_issue: "Un seguro que paga" is a faithful rendering; the English has no article issue but the Spanish mixes formal "usted" fine. Minor: 'Insurance' used without article, Spanish uses article; not a meaning change.

english: It covers the loan payments if you die, become disabled or lose your job. It is optional, often costs a lot for what it gives, and the price is added to the amount you borrow. Your existing life or disability insurance may already do the job.
spanish: Cubre los pagos del préstamo si usted fallece, queda discapacitado o pierde el empleo. Es opcional, muchas veces cuesta mucho para lo que da, y su precio se suma a lo que pide prestado. Su seguro de vida o de discapacidad actual quizá ya cumpla esa función.
back_translation: It covers loan payments if you die, become disabled, or lose your job. It is optional, often costs a lot for what it gives, and its price is added to what you borrow. Your current life or disability insurance may already fulfill that function.
screen_issue: "Quizá ya cumpla esa función" and "fallece" are a bit formal/literary for US Spanish but preserve meaning; "se suma a lo que pide prestado" fine. "Queda discapacitado" is slightly less common than "queda incapacitado" or "sufre una discapacidad"; understandable.

english: It can be an expensive way to cover a small risk.
spanish: Puede ser una forma cara de cubrir un riesgo pequeño.
back_translation: It can be an expensive way to cover a small risk.

english: What does this cost in total, what exactly does it pay, and can I say no without changing the loan?
spanish: ¿Cuánto cuesta en total, qué paga exactamente, y puedo decir que no sin cambiar el préstamo?
back_translation: How much does it cost in total, what exactly does it pay for, and can I say no without changing the loan?

english: Like buying an extra insurance on a phone you already have covered by your home policy.
spanish: Como comprar un seguro adicional para un teléfono que ya cubre la póliza de su casa.
back_translation: Like buying additional insurance for a phone that your home policy already covers.
screen_issue: Minor wording shift: 'your home policy' became 'la póliza de su casa' and back-translated as 'that your home policy already covers', which reads fine; 'extra insurance' vs 'seguro adicional' is equivalent.

english: Collision and comprehensive
spanish: Colisión y cobertura total
back_translation: Collision and comprehensive coverage
screen_issue: 'Comprehensive' is rendered as 'cobertura total', which a US Spanish reader may find less standard than 'cobertura integral' or 'cobertura amplia'; back-translation returns 'comprehensive coverage', so meaning is preserved.

english: The insurance that repairs or replaces your own car.
spanish: El seguro que repara o reemplaza su propio auto.
back_translation: The insurance that repairs or replaces your own car.

english: Collision pays to repair your car after a crash, whoever is at fault. Comprehensive pays for things that are not a crash: theft, fire, hail, a tree falling on the car. Lenders require both while you owe money. Each has a deductible you pay first.
spanish: La colisión paga la reparación de su auto después de un choque, sin importar quién tuvo la culpa. La cobertura total (comprehensive) paga lo que no es un choque: robo, incendio, granizo, un árbol que cae sobre el auto. Los prestamistas exigen ambas mientras usted deba dinero. Cada una tiene un deducible que usted paga primero.
back_translation: Collision pays for your car's repair after a crash, no matter who was at fault. Comprehensive coverage pays for what is not a crash: theft, fire, hail, a tree falling on the car. Lenders require both while you owe money. Each has a deductible that you pay first.
screen_issue: 'Comprehensive' appears as 'cobertura total (comprehensive)'; the English in parentheses is helpful but the term 'cobertura total' may be unfamiliar. 'Hail' as 'granizo' is correct. Back-translation is faithful.

english: They are in the lender's contract and add to your monthly cost of owning the car.
spanish: Están en el contrato del prestamista y suman al costo mensual de tener el auto.
back_translation: They are in the lender's contract and add to the monthly cost of having the car.

english: What will collision and comprehensive cost on this car with a deductible I can pay?
spanish: ¿Cuánto costarán la colisión y la cobertura total en este auto, con un deducible que yo pueda pagar?
back_translation: How much will collision and comprehensive coverage cost on this car, with a deductible I can afford?

english: Like insurance for your house: one part for accidents you cause, one for storms and theft.
spanish: Como el seguro de una casa: una parte para accidentes que usted causa, otra para tormentas y robos.
back_translation: Like home insurance: one part for accidents you cause, another for storms and thefts.
screen_issue: Back-translation 'another part for storms and thefts' drops the word 'one' distinction slightly but meaning holds; 'robos' vs 'thefts' is equivalent.

english: Liability coverage
spanish: Cobertura de responsabilidad civil
back_translation: Liability coverage

english: Insurance that pays for harm you cause to others.
spanish: Un seguro que paga el daño que usted causa a otros.
back_translation: Insurance that pays for damage you cause to others.
screen_issue: 'Harm' rendered as 'daño' and back-translated as 'damage'; 'daño' is accurate for US Spanish, minor nuance difference only.

english: If you cause a crash, liability pays for the other driver's repairs and medical bills, and for legal costs, up to your limits. Nearly every state requires it. The minimum is often low, so many people carry more.
spanish: Si usted causa un choque, la responsabilidad civil paga las reparaciones y los gastos médicos de la otra persona, y los costos legales, hasta sus límites. Casi todos los estados la exigen. El mínimo suele ser bajo, así que mucha gente lleva más.
back_translation: If you cause a crash, liability pays for the other person's repairs and medical expenses, and legal costs, up to its limits. Almost all states require it. The minimum is usually low, so many people carry more.
screen_issue: 'Liability' as 'responsabilidad civil' is the standard US Spanish insurance term, so acceptable; back-translation says 'legal costs' for 'gastos legales', fine. 'Medical bills' as 'gastos médicos' is correct.

english: A serious crash can cost far more than the legal minimum covers, and you pay the rest.
spanish: Un choque grave puede costar mucho más de lo que cubre el mínimo legal, y usted paga el resto.
back_translation: A serious crash can cost much more than the legal minimum covers, and you pay the rest.

english: How much liability coverage should I have for what I own, and what does a higher limit cost?
spanish: ¿Cuánta cobertura de responsabilidad civil debo tener para lo que poseo, y cuánto cuesta un límite más alto?
back_translation: How much liability coverage should I have for what I own, and how much does a higher limit cost?

english: Like the protection a homeowner has if a visitor is hurt on the property.
spanish: Como la protección que tiene el dueño de una casa si una visita se lastima en la propiedad.
back_translation: Like the protection a homeowner has if a visitor gets hurt on the property.
screen_issue: 'Homeowner' as 'el dueño de una casa' is accurate; 'visitor' as 'una visita' is a literal rendering that may be slightly unclear to a US reader, though it still reads naturally.

english: Uninsured motorist coverage
spanish: Cobertura contra conductor sin seguro
back_translation: Uninsured motorist coverage
screen_issue: 'Uninsured motorist' as 'conductor sin seguro' is clear; 'cobertura contra conductor sin seguro' is understandable, though 'cobertura por conductor sin seguro' is more common in US Spanish-language policies.

english: Pays you when the other driver has no insurance.
spanish: Le paga a usted cuando el otro conductor no tiene seguro.
back_translation: It pays you when the other driver does not have insurance.

english: If someone without insurance, or with too little, causes a crash, this coverage pays your bills. A hit-and-run driver is covered too. It is optional in many states and usually costs little.
spanish: Si alguien sin seguro, o con muy poco, causa un choque, esta cobertura paga sus gastos. También cubre a un conductor que se da a la fuga. En muchos estados es opcional y suele costar poco.
back_translation: If someone without insurance, or with very little, causes a crash, this coverage pays your expenses. It also covers a hit-and-run driver. In many states it is optional and usually costs little.
screen_issue: 'Hit-and-run driver' as 'un conductor que se da a la fuga' is standard and clear; 'con muy poco' is a slight intensification of 'too little' but meaning is preserved.

english: Many drivers have no insurance, and without it you may pay for their mistake.
spanish: Muchos conductores no tienen seguro, y sin esta cobertura usted podría pagar por el error de ellos.
back_translation: Many drivers do not have insurance, and without this coverage you could pay for their mistake.

english: How much would uninsured motorist coverage add to the premium, and is it required in this state?
spanish: ¿Cuánto sumaría a la prima la cobertura contra conductor sin seguro, y es obligatoria en este estado?
back_translation: How much would uninsured motorist coverage add to the premium, and is it mandatory in this state?

english: Like a spare key left with a neighbour. You hope you never need it, and it helps a lot the one time you do.
spanish: Como una llave de repuesto con un vecino. Espera no necesitarla, y ayuda mucho la única vez que la necesita.
back_translation: Like a spare key with a neighbor. You hope you do not need it, and it helps a lot the only time you do.

english: Appraisal
spanish: Avalúo
back_translation: Appraisal

english: The dealer's check of what your car is worth.
spanish: La revisión del concesionario de lo que vale su auto.
back_translation: The dealer's review of what your car is worth.
screen_issue: 'Review' for 'check' is a small wording shift; 'revisión' still conveys the evaluation sense.

english: The dealer looks at your car, its mileage and condition, and offers a value for the trade-in. Different dealers and online buyers will give different numbers. An appraisal is not a promise: the figure can change if the dealer finds something later.
spanish: El concesionario mira su auto, sus millas y su estado, y ofrece un valor por el intercambio. Distintos concesionarios y compradores en línea darán números distintos. Un avalúo no es una promesa: la cifra puede cambiar si el concesionario encuentra algo después.
back_translation: The dealer looks at your car, its miles, and its condition, and offers a value for the trade-in. Different dealers and online buyers will give different numbers. An appraisal is not a promise: the figure can change if the dealer finds something later.

english: It sets your trade-in allowance, so it deserves a second opinion.
spanish: Fija lo que le dan por su auto de intercambio, así que merece una segunda opinión.
back_translation: It sets what they give you for your trade-in car, so it deserves a second opinion.

english: Will you put this appraisal in writing, and how long does it last?
spanish: ¿Pone este avalúo por escrito, y cuánto tiempo es válido?
back_translation: Do you put this appraisal in writing, and how long is it valid?

english: Like getting a quote on a second-hand bike. Three shops give three prices.
spanish: Como pedir presupuesto por una bicicleta usada. Tres tiendas dan tres precios.
back_translation: Like asking for a quote for a used bicycle. Three stores give three prices.

english: Wholesale and retail value
spanish: Valor mayorista y valor al público
back_translation: Wholesale value and retail value

english: What a dealer pays for a car, and what it sells for.
spanish: Lo que un concesionario paga por un auto, y por cuánto lo vende.
back_translation: What a dealer pays for a car, and for how much they sell it.

english: Wholesale is the price at which dealers buy cars from each other and at auctions. Retail is the higher price at which they sell to the public. A dealer offering you the wholesale price for your trade-in is giving you less than they will ask for the same car.
spanish: El valor mayorista es el precio al que los concesionarios se compran autos entre sí y en subastas. El valor al público es el precio más alto al que los venden. Si un concesionario le ofrece el precio mayorista por su auto de intercambio, le da menos de lo que pedirá por el mismo auto.
back_translation: The wholesale value is the price at which dealers buy cars from each other and at auctions. The retail value is the highest price at which they sell them. If a dealer offers you the wholesale price for your trade-in car, they are giving you less than what they will ask for the same car.

english: It shows why a trade-in offer is lower than what you see cars like yours selling for.
spanish: Explica por qué una oferta por su auto es menor que lo que ve que cuestan autos como el suyo.
back_translation: It explains why an offer for your car is less than what you see cars like yours cost.

english: What is the wholesale value of my car, and what will you sell it for?
spanish: ¿Cuál es el valor mayorista de mi auto, y por cuánto lo van a vender?
back_translation: What is the wholesale value of my car, and for how much are they going to sell it?

english: Like a fruit stall that buys crates from the market and sells single pieces at a higher price.
spanish: Como un puesto de fruta que compra cajas en el mercado y vende piezas sueltas a un precio mayor.
back_translation: Like a fruit stand that buys boxes at the market and sells loose pieces at a higher price.
screen_issue: 'Puesto de fruta' and 'piezas sueltas' are accurate; 'puesto' is a regional-leaning word for a stall but understood in US Spanish. Minor wording difference only.

english: Trade-in tax credit
spanish: Crédito de impuesto por intercambio
back_translation: Trade-in tax credit

english: In many states, you pay sales tax only on the difference.
spanish: En muchos estados, usted paga impuesto solo sobre la diferencia.
back_translation: In many states, you pay tax only on the difference.
screen_issue: Source says 'sales tax'; 'impuesto' alone drops the 'sobre la venta' qualifier. Meaning is mostly kept but slightly less precise than the original.

english: In many states, the value of your trade-in is taken off the price before sales tax is worked out. So a trade-in can lower your tax as well as your price. Some states do not do this, and rules differ. The contract shows how tax was worked out.
spanish: En muchos estados, el valor de su auto de intercambio se resta del precio antes de calcular el impuesto sobre la venta. Así, el intercambio puede bajar su impuesto además de su precio. Algunos estados no lo hacen, y las reglas varían. El contrato muestra cómo se calculó el impuesto.
back_translation: In many states, the value of your trade-in car is subtracted from the price before calculating the sales tax. Thus, the trade-in can lower your tax in addition to your price. Some states do not do this, and the rules vary. The contract shows how the tax was calculated.

english: It can be a real saving that a private sale would not give you.
spanish: Puede ser un ahorro real que una venta privada no le daría.
back_translation: It can be a real saving that a private sale would not give you.

english: In this state, is sales tax worked out after my trade-in is taken off, and can you show me on the sheet?
spanish: En este estado, ¿el impuesto se calcula después de restar mi auto de intercambio, y puede mostrármelo en la hoja?
back_translation: In this state, is the tax calculated after subtracting my trade-in car, and can you show it to me on the sheet?

english: Like a store that charges tax on what you pay after a trade-in coupon, not before it.
spanish: Como una tienda que cobra impuesto sobre lo que paga después de un cupón de intercambio, no antes.
back_translation: Like a store that charges tax on what you pay after a trade-in coupon, not before.

english: Total loss
spanish: Pérdida total
back_translation: Total loss

english: When the car is declared not worth fixing.
spanish: Cuando el auto se declara que no vale la pena repararlo.
back_translation: When the car is declared not worth repairing.
screen_issue: 'Reparar' is correct; back-translation reads 'repairing' against 'fixing'. Small wording difference only, no change in meaning.

english: After a bad crash, theft or flood, the insurer may decide the repair costs more than the car is worth. It then pays the car's value, not the cost of the loan. If you owe more than that value, you still owe the rest, unless you have GAP coverage.
spanish: Después de un choque grave, un robo o una inundación, la aseguradora puede decidir que reparar cuesta más de lo que vale el auto. Entonces paga el valor del auto, no el saldo del préstamo. Si usted debe más que ese valor, todavía debe el resto, a menos que tenga cobertura GAP.
back_translation: After a serious crash, a theft, or a flood, the insurer can decide that repairing costs more than the car is worth. Then it pays the value of the car, not the loan balance. If you owe more than that value, you still owe the rest, unless you have GAP coverage.
screen_issue: 'Desastre' omitted but fine; 'walk away' rendered as 'se va sin más' is slightly less clear but meaning intact. Note: the Spanish says 'la compañía' for the insurer context which is accurate.

english: It is exactly the moment when owing more than the car is worth costs you money.
spanish: Es justo el momento en que deber más de lo que vale el auto le cuesta dinero.
back_translation: It is just the moment when owing more than the car is worth costs you money.
screen_issue: 'It is exactly the moment' rendered as 'justo el momento', a slight nuance shift toward 'just'; meaning preserved.

english: If the car were a total loss in the first year, what would insurance pay and what would I still owe?
spanish: Si el auto fuera pérdida total en el primer año, ¿qué pagaría el seguro y cuánto seguiría debiendo?
back_translation: If the car were a total loss in the first year, what would the insurance pay and how much would you still owe?

english: Like an old phone that is damaged beyond repair. The shop gives you what it was worth, not what you paid.
spanish: Como un teléfono viejo dañado sin arreglo. La tienda le da lo que valía, no lo que usted pagó.
back_translation: Like an old damaged phone beyond repair. The store gives you what it was worth, not what you paid.
screen_issue: 'Beyond repair' rendered as 'sin arreglo' is clear; minor wording difference.

english: Closed-end lease
spanish: Arrendamiento de plazo cerrado
back_translation: Closed-end lease

english: The usual lease. You hand the car back at the end.
spanish: El arrendamiento común. Usted devuelve el auto al final.
back_translation: The common lease. You return the car at the end.

english: In a closed-end lease the maker sets the car's value at the end in advance, and you walk away if you stay within the miles and keep the car in good condition. If it is worth less than expected, that is the lessor's risk. You still pay for extra miles and damage.
spanish: En un arrendamiento de plazo cerrado, el valor del auto al final lo fija de antemano la compañía, y usted se va sin más si se mantuvo dentro de las millas y cuidó el auto. Si vale menos de lo esperado, ese riesgo es de la compañía. Aun así paga por millas extra y daños.
back_translation: In a closed-end lease, the value of the car at the end is set beforehand by the company, and you leave without further ado if you stayed within the miles and took care of the car. If it is worth less than expected, that risk is the company's. You still pay for extra miles and damages.

screen_issue: 'Dura más de seis años' back-translates as 'last more than six years', which matches 'run longer than six years'. 'Casi un tercio' matches 'nearly one third'. The figure and source are preserved; the Spanish 'almost' versus 'nearly' is a trivial difference. Note the register is not an issue since no pronoun is used.

english: The fees are on the high side
spanish: Los cargos están algo altos
back_translation: The fees are somewhat high
screen_issue: 'Algo altos' back-translates as 'somewhat high', a softer reading than 'on the high side' in the original, though close in meaning.

english: Fees are ⟦1⟧. Dealer document fees often run a few hundred dollars, and some states cap them.
spanish: Los cargos son ⟦1⟧. Los cargos por documentos del concesionario suelen ser de unos cientos de dólares, y algunos estados los limitan.
back_translation: The fees are ⟦1⟧. Dealer document fees are usually a few hundred dollars, and some states limit them.
screen_issue: 'Unos cientos de dólares' back-translates as 'a few hundred dollars', matching 'a few hundred dollars'. 'Los cargos son ⟦1⟧' is consistent. 'Algunos estados los limitan' matches 'some states cap them' in meaning; 'limitan' is adequate, though 'los topan' is more colloquial and less common than 'limitan' in US Spanish. Placeholder preserved.

english: Can you list each fee and what it is for?
spanish: ¿Puede listar cada cargo y para qué es?
back_translation: Can you list each fee and what it is for?
screen_issue: '¿Puede listar cada cargo y para qué es?' is a shift to a colloquial 'para qué es' and uses 'listar', which back-translates as 'list' correctly. However, the question form 'para qué es' may read as informal; a more standard phrasing would be '¿Puede enumerar cada cargo y explicar para qué sirve?' to match the 'what it is for' sense. The text remains polite in register since it uses 'puede' with the formal form, so no register flag.

english: Consumer guides and state rules differ; check your state's attorney general or motor vehicle site.
spanish: Las guías al consumidor y las reglas estatales varían; revise el sitio de la fiscalía general o del departamento de vehículos de su estado.
back_translation: Consumer guides and state rules vary; check your state attorney general or department of motor vehicles website.
screen_issue: "attorney general" translated as "fiscalía general"; in US Spanish "procuraduría" or "fiscal general del estado" is more common, and "vehículos" for motor vehicles is fine. Minor terminology only.

back_translation: The extras cost ⟦1⟧, and about ⟦2⟧ when counting tax and interest. That is about ⟦3⟧ of your monthly payments.
screen_issue: "Eso es cerca de" vs "That is about" is fine; "al contar" is a slightly looser rendering of "when counting" but meaning holds. Placeholders preserved.

back_translation: If I did not ask for an extra, can you remove it? Which ones can I cancel later?

back_translation: CFPB and Consumer Reports: you do not have to pay for an extra you did not ask for.
screen_issue: "un extra" is a common US Spanish term; "add-on" is rendered as "extra" consistently with the rest. Meaning unchanged.

back_translation: The payment does not match the numbers

screen_issue: "sale a" for "comes to/comes out to" is an acceptable colloquial rendering; "lo que dan los números" is slightly awkward but meaning is preserved. Placeholders preserved.

back_translation: FTC: “payment packing” hides extras inside a monthly figure.
screen_issue: "payment packing" is kept in English inside quotes; a US Spanish reader may not know the term, so an explanation would help. Otherwise accurate.

english: You owe more than the trade is worth

back_translation: You owe more than your trade-in car is worth
screen_issue: "auto de intercambio" is a literal, less common term; "auto a cambiar" or "auto usado que entrega como parte de pago" is what US Spanish readers would recognize. Meaning intact.

english: The gap is ⟦1⟧. It is added to the new loan, and you pay interest on it.

back_translation: The difference is ⟦1⟧. It is added to the new loan, and you pay interest on it.

back_translation: How much of the new loan is the old loan I still owe?

back_translation: FTC, Financing or Leasing a Car: negative equity is added to the new loan.
screen_issue: "capital negativo" is a literal rendering of "negative equity"; US Spanish readers more often see "deuda pendiente" or "saldo a favor del prestamista". Meaning is preserved but the term may confuse.

english: ⟦1⟧% is a higher rate
spanish: ⟦1⟧% es una tasa alta
back_translation: ⟦1⟧% is a high rate
screen_issue: "una tasa alta" for "a higher rate" drops the comparative sense (higher than what, or than normal); the English is also an incomplete fragment, so the Spanish matches its wording. Slight nuance loss.

english: Rates depend on your credit and the lender. A dealer can add to the rate a lender offers, and the extra interest goes to the dealer.
spanish: Las tasas dependen de su crédito y del prestamista. Un concesionario puede sumar a la tasa que ofrece un prestamista, y el interés extra se queda con el concesionario.
back_translation: Rates depend on your credit and the lender. A dealership can add to the rate a lender offers, and the extra interest stays with the dealership.
screen_issue: "se queda con el concesionario" is a loose rendering of "stays with the dealership"; it is understandable but could read as the dealer keeping the car or money in an unclear way. Also "sumar a la tasa" is acceptable. Possible nuance concern about who receives the extra interest.

english: What rate did the lender approve me for, and is any of this rate added by the dealership?
spanish: ¿Qué tasa me aprobó el prestamista, y el concesionario agregó algo a esta tasa?
back_translation: What rate did the lender approve me for, and did the dealership add anything to this rate?
screen_issue: The English asks whether the dealership added anything to the rate; the back-translation is a question about whether the dealership added to it, but the Spanish uses "agregó algo a esta tasa" in the past tense, which is a slight shift from present-tense ask. Meaning close, but the question could be read as a past-event statement rather than a question about the current deal. Also "tasa me aprobó" is somewhat unnatural.

english: CFPB and the Center for Responsible Lending: dealer rate markups.

back_translation: CFPB and the Center for Responsible Lending: dealership markups on the rate.
screen_issue: "sobrecargos" is a literal and less common term for dealer markups in US Spanish; "sobrecargos" may also read as airline flight attendants. Meaning preserved.

english: No sales tax is counted

back_translation: Sales tax is not counted
screen_issue: The English heading "No sales tax is counted" is rendered as "No se cuenta impuesto sobre la venta", which is clear; the back-translation adds "Sales tax is not counted", a minor passive shift. Acceptable.

english: The tax rate is zero, so the out-the-door price here has no sales tax in it. Most states charge it on a car.

back_translation: The tax rate is zero, so the final price here does not include sales tax. Most states charge it on a car.
screen_issue: "la mayoría de los estados lo cobran en un auto" is slightly awkward ("en un auto" vs "sobre un auto"), and "precio final" for "out-the-door price" is less specific; US Spanish readers may prefer "precio total con todo incluido". Meaning preserved.

english: What is the sales tax in dollars on this deal?

back_translation: How much is the sales tax in dollars in this deal?

screen_issue: 'hoja' is a literal rendering of 'worksheet' but in US Spanish 'hoja' alone reads as 'sheet of paper'; the form-type meaning is lost. Also the imperative 'Ingrese' is polite-form (usted), which is correct, but 'the tax from the worksheet' is reduced to 'la hoja de [the] sheet tax', changing meaning to something unclear. Consider 'Ingrese el impuesto de la hoja de cálculo.'
